title: DMET results
text:
Preface
This book collects results from a pharmacogenomics screen of 27 drug-metabolizing enzyme and transporter (DMET) proteins measured across Collaborative Cross (CC) mouse strains. The current integrated v2 report excludes CES2 because of a protein QC issue; its legacy chapter is retained in the source tree but omitted from the rendered book.
The V2 results overview is the reporting-focused cross-panel summary, with the updated summary table, QTL maps, heritability results, protein clustering, and transcriptome figures. The Analysis progress page records current coverage and outstanding analyses. The remaining protein chapters provide detailed, protein-specific results where available. These include:

Protein distributions – raw, RINT-normalized, and Box-Cox-transformed measurements, and which transformation was recommended.
Heritability – how strongly the trait clusters within CC strains.
pQTL genome scans – miqtl-based linkage scans, with permutation-derived significance thresholds.
RNA mediation – whether transcript abundance (via bmediatR) explains the protein QTL.
Merge / diplotype fine-mapping – founder-haplotype-resolved fine-mapping at significant loci.
TIMBR – whether the founder haplotypes at a QTL collapse into fewer functional alleles.

Not every protein has been carried through every stage yet. Rather than hide that, each chapter says explicitly which analyses exist for that protein and which don’t (“Not yet analyzed here”), and the Analysis Status chapter gives the full picture across all 27 proteins at once, plus a short list of known data-quality issues in the current figures. That chapter is regenerated automatically (via build_chapters.py) from what’s actually present on disk, so it should never drift out of date the way a hand-maintained checklist would.
See Methods for how the underlying proteomics and genetic data were generated.

title: Methods
text:
Proteomics
Raw protein-abundance data were generated using protein isolation, proteolytic digestion, and quantitative targeted absolute proteomics (QTAP) analysis, as previously described in Qasem et al. (2020). Peptides were selected to avoid confounding from genetic variation, by excluding peptides with non-synonymous mutations predicted from the Inbred Strain Variant Database (Oreper et al., 2017).
For three proteins – Cyp2c50, Cyp3a11, and Oatp1a4 – avoiding a variant peptide was not possible, and the peptide sequence used contains a missense variant across some Collaborative Cross founder/strain haplotypes. Separately, Cyp2c39 likely carries a genetic variant in the C57BL/6J (B6) strain that caused QTAP to fail to detect the protein in B6-descended strains; this shows up as a zero-inflated phenotype for Cyp2c39 (see that chapter’s distribution plots).

title: Methods
text:
Genome scans
pQTL genome scans were run with miqtl. Genome-wide significance thresholds were derived from permutation testing (typically 1000 permutations) using a generalized extreme value (GEV) fit to the permuted maximum statistics, at the 0.90/0.95 percentile as noted per chapter.

title: Methods
text:
RNA mediation
Mediation analysis uses bmediatR (Bayesian mediation analysis for QTL) to test whether transcript abundance mediates a protein QTL, and whether one protein mediates another’s QTL at a shared peak locus.

title: Methods
text:
TIMBR
TIMBR (Tree-based Inference of Multiple-allele Regression) infers whether the founder haplotypes underlying a QTL collapse into fewer functional alleles, using a Chinese Restaurant Process prior over haplotype groupings with a phylogenetic backbone, rather than assuming every founder haplotype is functionally distinct.

title: Methods
text:
Merge / diplotype fine-mapping
At significant loci, diplotype-resolved (“merge”) analysis re-tests association at the level of imputed founder-haplotype dosage to narrow the candidate region and flag significant SNPs. As of this writing this has only been carried out for a subset of proteins – see Analysis Status.






Note



Full bibliographic details for Qasem et al. (2020) and Oreper et al. (2017) are not yet recorded anywhere in this project. Please add the complete citations to references.bib – these are currently referenced by author/year only.

title: V2 results overview
text:
Cross-protein summary
This is the reporting overview for the rerun_2026-09-24_v2 rerun. It presents the current cross-protein results and links the figure set. The reporting table and figures exclude CES2 because of the previously identified protein QC issue. CES2’s legacy source chapter is omitted from the rendered book; this page is the cross-panel summary.
The table combines pQTL lead-locus statistics and protein broad-sense H² with coding-transcript broad-sense H² where an original-array probe could be matched. Protein H² uses the Box–Cox transformed protein measurements supplied to the QTL analyses. Transcript H² uses RINT-transformed individual RNA array measurements, with CC line as a random effect and scan date adjusted as a fixed effect. Transcript rows without a gene-specific match are shown as unavailable.
Download the QC-filtered CSV summary or the transcript H² estimates and intervals. OCT1.2 is retained with its protein H² estimate from the figure 2 results, but the v2 integrated table contains no OCT1.2 pQTL row.

Protein broad-sense H² and clustered Box–Cox protein profiles. Strains are ordered by the gap-statistic k=3 assignment.


Protein H² is estimated from replicated protein measurements. The figure displays the protein-level estimates and their uncertainty alongside the strain-level expression heatmap. The separately estimated transcript H² values are summarized in the table above; they are not the estimates in this forest panel.

Coding-transcript heritability



Broad-sense heritability estimates for the coding transcripts mapped to the protein panel.


Transcript H² was estimated from RINT-transformed individual RNA measurements for 19 unique original-array probes, corresponding to 20 protein rows. The model includes a random CC-line effect and adjusts for scan date; intervals are 95% parametric-bootstrap intervals. The table gives the per-transcript BH-adjusted p-values.


Protein phenotype correlation



Descriptive across-strain Pearson correlations between protein abundance measurements.


This descriptive Pearson matrix summarizes observed across-strain protein abundance and is distinct from the random-effect covariance estimates below.


Genetic covariance and genetic correlation



Protein genetic correlations, with broad-sense H² on the diagonal.





Coding-transcript genetic correlations, with broad-sense H² on the diagonal.


Download the protein genetic covariance matrix, protein genetic correlation matrix with H² diagonal, coding-transcript covariance matrix, or coding-transcript correlation matrix with H² diagonal. The displayed diagonal contains the existing broad-sense H² estimates; off-diagonal cells are estimated CC-line genetic correlations. Covariances use Box–Cox protein values and RINT transcript values. Protein residual cross-trait covariance is assumed zero because replicate assays are not paired across traits; transcript off-diagonal covariance is corrected for within-line residual covariance. Correlations were projected to a valid correlation matrix after sampling correction. Estimates are point estimates without confidence intervals.

title: V2 results overview
text:
Remaining reporting gaps

Genetic covariance uncertainty: current covariance and correlation matrices are point estimates; confidence intervals or bootstrap uncertainty are not yet estimated.
eQTL positional annotation: 20,666/20,666 transcripts have peak results, while 19,959 are plotted because 707 lack complete position annotation.
Coding transcript matching: six of the 26 QC-retained protein rows lack a gene-specific original-array transcript match, so their transcript H² is not estimated.
OCT1.2 pQTL: its protein H² is available, but the v2 integrated summary and per-protein scan figure are absent.
Mediation and fine mapping: mediation covers seven reportable proteins from the targeted array. Merge/diplotype results remain locus-specific follow-up, not a uniform panel-wide report.

title: Analysis progress
text:
Reporting interpretation
This page tracks the reporting status of the rerun_2026-09-24_v2 results bundle. The cross-panel plots and integrated summary are in V2 results overview. CES2 is excluded from reporting analyses because of its protein QC issue.
The completed plots support reporting protein-level heritability, strain variation, protein QTL signals, complete transcript peak results, near-complete positional eQTL mapping, and targeted mediation. The current pQTL table is incomplete for OCT1.2. Genetic covariance estimates are available but currently lack uncertainty intervals.
